title: The site's own safety procedures and your supervisor come first
applies_when: Always. Whenever a step, a pack or Hadley says anything that differs from the site's own safety procedures, permits or the supervisor's instructions, the site wins.
words_shown: Your site's own safety rules and your supervisor's instructions come first. If anything here is different from them, follow the site, not this. Stop now. Go to your site supervisor or engineer.

sources.title: HSE: Electrical safety at work, frequently asked questions (follow the maker's instructions and local safety rules)
OSHA: Green Job Hazards, Solar Energy

title: A panel is live whenever light falls on it
applies_when: A step has you touch, cut, strip, open or test any wire, terminal or bare metal of a panel, a string or its wiring. A panel makes voltage in daylight, even in cloud, and its DC side stays live when the inverter or the mains is switched off.
words_shown: Stop. Treat every panel and its wiring as live in daylight. Switching off the inverter or the mains does not make it safe. Do not touch, cut or test it yourself. Go to your site supervisor or engineer.

sources.title: Ontario: Firefighter guidance note 6-34, solar photovoltaic systems (panels stay energised while light reaches them)
OSHA: Green Job Hazards, Solar Energy, Electrical
OSHA: Green Job Hazards, Solar Energy, Lockout/Tagout (cover panels; verify isolation before work)
HSE: Electrical safety at work, frequently asked questions (prove conductors dead before work)

ghost_to_confirm: Whether measuring a voltage with a meter is a stop for the newest contractor. The draft says yes (the triggers 'multimeter', 'measure the voltage'), because a meter on a live string is live work; if crews are trained to measure, this trigger will stop many troubleshooting flows.

title: Never pull connectors apart while current can flow
applies_when: A step has you unplug, separate or disconnect a panel's connectors, a string or a DC lead. Pulling a connector apart under load can draw an arc that burns.
words_shown: Stop. Do not pull the connectors apart. Under load they can spark and burn you. The system must be made safe first, by someone allowed to do it. Go to your site supervisor or engineer.

sources.title: Staubli: MC4 branch connector assembly instructions MA250 (never disconnect under load)
Staubli: assembly instructions MA263 (de-energise before mating or unmating)

ghost_to_confirm: Whether plugging a connector together (not only pulling one apart) is also a stop. The draft stops only on disconnecting; the makers' instructions say to de-energise before both.

title: Do not open an inverter, combiner, battery or other electrical enclosure
applies_when: A step has you open, unscrew or take the cover off an inverter, combiner box, junction box, isolator, fuse holder, battery cabinet, switchboard or any other box that holds wiring.
words_shown: Stop. Do not open this box. Parts inside can stay live and hold a charge even when switched off. Only someone authorised may open it. Go to your site supervisor or engineer.

sources.title: HSE: Electrical safety at work, frequently asked questions (isolate, lock off, release stored energy, prove dead; competence)
OSHA: Green Job Hazards, Solar Energy, Lockout/Tagout (only authorised employees lock out equipment)

title: Work at height or on a roof
applies_when: A step has you go onto a roof, a ladder, a scaffold or a frame, or near an edge, skylight or roof hatch, or carry a panel up. There is no safe height to fall from; the site sets the fall protection.
words_shown: Stop. Do not go up or near an edge until your supervisor has shown you the fall protection for this job and it is in place. Never climb a ladder carrying a panel. Go to your site supervisor or engineer.

sources.title: OSHA: Green Job Hazards, Solar Energy, Falls
HSE: Work at height

title: Keep well away from overhead power lines
applies_when: A step has you work, lift a panel, raise a ladder or move a tool or machine anywhere near an overhead power line.
words_shown: Stop. Do not work, lift or raise anything near an overhead power line. It can kill without being touched. Go to your site supervisor or engineer.

sources.title: OSHA: Green Job Hazards, Solar Energy, Electrical (keep at least 10 feet from overhead lines)

ghost_to_confirm: This rule is beyond the brief's list (added because OSHA names overhead lines among solar workers' electrical hazards). The words give no distance: the site's own distance applies (OSHA's is at least 10 feet). Keep, change or drop.

title: Damaged, burnt, melted, wet or corroded parts
applies_when: A connector, cable, panel or box is cracked, cut, crushed, burnt, scorched, melted, discoloured, corroded, wet inside, or has copper showing, or a connector does not lock or does not match its other half.
words_shown: Stop. Do not touch, use or reconnect a damaged, burnt, melted, wet or corroded part. It can be live and can start a fire. Keep others away. Go to your site supervisor or engineer.

sources.title: UK government (BRE): Fire incidents involving solar panels (connectors and poor installation among the causes)
Staubli: MC4 branch connector assembly instructions MA250

title: Heat, a burning smell, smoke, sparks or arcing
applies_when: Anything is hotter than it should be, smells of burning, smokes, sparks, crackles, buzzes or shows an arc or flame.
words_shown: Stop. Step back and do not touch it. Keep others away. If there is fire or smoke, follow the site's emergency procedure. Go to your site supervisor or engineer.

sources.title: UK government (BRE): Fire incidents involving solar panels (electrical arcing the likely ignition)
OSHA: Green Job Hazards, Solar Energy, Electrical (arc flash)

title: An earth (ground) fault or an electric shock
applies_when: A device shows an earth fault, ground fault, insulation or isolation fault, or a protective device trips; or someone feels a tingle or a shock from a frame, panel or box. A fault can make metal live that should not be.
words_shown: Stop. Do not touch the frames, panels or boxes. A fault may have made metal live. If someone has had a shock, call for help and first aid at once, and do not touch them while they may still be touching it. Go to your site supervisor or engineer.

sources.title: Fluke: What is a DC ground fault in a PV system?
OSHA: Green Job Hazards, Solar Energy, Electrical (shock and burns when connecting panels)

ghost_to_confirm: The first-aid sentence (call for help, do not touch a person who may still be touching something live) is common first-aid practice but none of the sources above states it; the site's own first-aid arrangements apply. Keep, reword or source it. The same goes for SR-08's line to follow the site's emergency procedure on fire or smoke.

title: A voltage above what a device is rated for
applies_when: The panels' voltage, or the string's, is or could be above the device's highest input voltage, or a step adds panels in series. A panel's voltage rises in the cold, so a string that fits on a warm day may not on a cold morning.
words_shown: Stop. Do not connect. Too high a voltage can destroy the device and start a fire, and panels give more volts when cold. Go to your site supervisor or engineer.

sources.title: Victron Energy: SmartSolar MPPT 150/70 to 250/100 manual, technical specifications (absolute maximum PV voltage in the coldest conditions)

title: Batteries
applies_when: A step has you connect, disconnect or work on battery terminals, battery cables or a battery bank; or a battery is swollen, hot, leaking, hissing or smells.
words_shown: Stop. Do not work on battery terminals or cables, and keep away from a battery that is swollen, hot, leaking, hissing or smells. A battery can burn, explode or give off toxic gas, and it cannot be switched off. Go to your site supervisor or engineer.

sources.title: OSHA: Lithium-ion Battery Safety, Hazards (heat, venting gas or smoke; toxic gases)

title: Never bypass or switch off a protective device
applies_when: A step has you bypass, bridge, remove, tape over or switch off a fuse, breaker, isolator, RCD, earth connection, shutdown switch or other protective device so that something works.
words_shown: Stop. Never bypass, bridge or switch off a fuse, breaker, isolator or other safety device to make something work. Go to your site supervisor or engineer.

title: A step that disagrees with the maker's instructions or the site's procedures
applies_when: A step says something different from the maker's manual, the label on the equipment or the site's own procedures, or two instructions disagree.
words_shown: Stop. If this step is different from the maker's instructions, the label or your site's procedures, do not do it. Go to your site supervisor or engineer.

sources.title: HSE: Electrical safety at work, frequently asked questions (follow the maker's instructions and local safety rules)

title: When you are unsure
applies_when: The worker is not sure what to do, has not been trained for the step, or what they see does not look like the step says it should.
words_shown: Stop. If you are not sure, do not guess. It is always right to stop and ask. Go to your site supervisor or engineer.
